mechanisms.chain: Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatment affects the tryptophan microenvironment around ferritin channels, decreases alpha-helix/beta-sheet contents, and lowers aromatic surface hydrophobicity and thermal stability, thereby facilitating dissociation into subunits at a more benign pH (pH 4.0) for guest molecule encapsulation.
mechanisms.claim: Atmospheric cold plasma (ACP) treatment modifies the structure and properties of ferritin to allow subunit dissociation and reassembly at a milder pH (pH 4.0) for encapsulation.

mechanisms.chain: Pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment modifies the structure and features of ferritin, enabling it to dissociate at a milder pH (pH 3.6) for encapsulation.
mechanisms.claim: Pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment modifies ferritin structure to allow dissociation at a milder pH (pH 3.6).

mechanisms.chain: Manothermosonication (MTS) treatment decreases ferritin stability, affecting iron oxidative deposition and release activity, allowing apoferritin to encapsulate EGCG via a benign pH conversion (pH 3.0/6.8).
mechanisms.claim: MTS treatment decreases ferritin stability and allows encapsulation of guest molecules via mild pH conversion.

mechanisms.chain: Temperature changes (heating up to 60 °C) can expand the fourfold channels of phytoferritin, as evidenced by an increased initial iron release rate and decreased alpha-helix content, allowing guest molecules to be loaded through channel expansion and recovery.
mechanisms.claim: Thermal treatment at up to 60 °C expands the fourfold channels of phytoferritin to allow cargo loading.

mechanisms.chain: High hydrostatic pressure (HHP) treatment (200–300 MPa) impairs hydrophobic interactions and changes tertiary and quaternary structure to encapsulate DOX into human H-chain ferritin without protein precipitation.
mechanisms.claim: High hydrostatic pressure alters protein conformation by impairing hydrophobic interactions to allow encapsulation.

named_proteins.name: recombinant human H-chain ferritin H alpha and H beta

mechanisms.chain: ELP fusion tags and elastin-like polypeptides
mechanisms.claim: Elastin-like polypeptides undergo a reversible inverse phase transition (co-acervation/self-aggregation) from soluble protein into insoluble hydrophobic aggregates (forming beta-spiral structures with type II beta-turns) when heated above their transition temperature (Tt), or through high local concentrations in the ER, leading to the formation of protein bodies.

named_proteins.name: tobacco immunoglobulin heavy chain binding protein

mechanisms.chain: α-synuclein fused to the GFP11 sensor fragment co-expressed with the GFP1–10 detector fragment
mechanisms.claim: Fluorescence complementation is directly proportional to α-synuclein solubility because the small GFP11 sensor fragment can only complement with the large GFP1–10 detector fragment if α-synuclein escapes aggregation and remains soluble, exposing the sensor fragment to the solvent.

mechanisms.chain: Direct MinE membrane interaction restrains MinE's capacity to stimulate MinD's ATPase activity, which regulates the detachment of MinD from the membrane and the wavelength/length scale of Min protein patterns.
mechanisms.claim: Impairing MinE membrane interaction (via truncation or single mutations in the membrane targeting sequence) increases MinD ATPase stimulation and reduces the lower limit of the concentration-dependent wavelength.

mechanisms.chain: Electrostatic interactions / ionic steering between positively charged residues / surface regions and the negatively charged backbone of DNA
mechanisms.claim: Interactions between Pa DpsL and DNA result in nicking, linearization, and degradation of plasmid DNA, mediated by electrostatic interactions/ionic steering.
measurable_properties: Binding affinity or interaction strength under varying ionic strength conditions
